summary: This engagement makes Pipeline.dispatch the only path from a transport to BackingStore in production code. It does NOT redesign Pipeline, MiddlewareRegistry, MiddlewareContext, HookDispatcher, or AuthMiddleware — those are stable, tested, and shipped. It WIRES them. Phase 02 (build-stdio) extends mcp_server/server.py's lifespan to construct `pipeline = build_default_pipeline(verifier=..., store=...)` once, stash it in `lifespan_result['pipeline']`, and then converts every one of the 15 tool handlers in mcp_server/tools.py from `await store.<op>(...)` calls into `await pipeline.dispatch(operation=..., input=..., connection_id=..., metadata={'_connection_credential': _resolve_credential(ctx)})`. A new `_resolve_credential(ctx)` helper builds a SignedRequest from MCP launch params (legacy compat: also accepts a bare agent_id when `SOX_AGENT_ID_SOURCE` selected the env-var path). Phase 03 (build-http) introduces a `build_app(store, pipeline, *, identity=None)` factory in transports/http/server.py, plumbs `pipeline` to `register_operation_routes`, and replaces the `_auth_and_body` + `await store.<op>(...)` pattern in all 22 routes (op_send/recv/subscribe/unsubscribe/list_channels/channels_ack/channels_heartbeat/channels_collect/replay/list_agents/group_create/group_invite/group_join/group_leave/group_list_members and any helper routes) with a single `await pipeline.dispatch(...)` call; `auth.py` is reduced from 125 LOC to ~5 LOC of `extract_bearer_token` only — `IdentityResolver` Protocol, `PassthroughIdentityResolver`, and `resolve_agent_id` all DELETED. Per analysis §5.4 the `applies_to.transports` problem is solved by constructing per-transport pipelines at load time; both transports share the default registry by default but tests can pin different sets.
summary_continued: Phase 04 (observability) generalises AuthMiddleware's existing `_record_timing` mechanism into a per-plugin trace emission performed by Pipeline base. Pipeline.dispatch wraps every plugin invocation in a timing window and appends a structured record `{plugin_id, kind, started_at, finished_at, verdict, error_code?, correlation_id}` to `ctx._meta['pipeline_trace']`. The `correlation_id` is echoed from the existing frozen `MiddlewareContext.correlation_id` field. The legacy `middleware_timings` array is left untouched for one release as a back-compat shim emitted alongside; v1.1 will drop it. AuthMiddleware's bespoke `_record_timing` calls become no-ops or are removed. Phase 05 (concurrency-fix) wraps verifier.py:198-223's prune+nonce-check+nonce-insert sequence in `async with self._lock:` (where `self._lock = asyncio.Lock()` initialised in `__init__`). Phase 06 (delete-harness-substitution) deletes tools/conformance_runner.py:805-813 (the `_registered_agents` substitution block plus the comment 'This mirrors the middleware layer...'), removes the `_registered_agents` field from SharedMemoryTarget, AND in the same commit edits .github/workflows/conformance.yml to uncomment the `python-reference-http` matrix line and rename the matrix entry to `conformance-substitution-removed` (no `conformance-legacy` mode is added — there is no rollback hatch). Phase 07 ships a new conformance fixture asserting that an unregistered-credential rejection arrives via a sox-error envelope from the server (not synthesised client-side). Phase 08 is review.
summary_continued_2: The phase ordering honours NR-1: phases 06 and 07 MAY land before 04 and 05 once 01/02/03 are complete. The file-dependency graph is built so phase 06's edits (conformance_runner.py + conformance.yml + the new fixture file) do NOT depend on phase 04's pipeline.py edits — phase 04 only changes the *content* of metadata that conformance fixtures already consume opaquely; phase 06 only changes whether the harness short-circuits. The credential-format question (bearer-token-as-agent-id vs SignedRequest header) is per-transport: stdio reads launch params (already half-wired in core/identity/middleware.py and AuthMiddleware), HTTP accepts a bearer token in `Authorization: Bearer <agent_id>` for legacy compat AND an optional `X-Sox-Signed-Request` header carrying a base64'd SignedRequest envelope for forward-compat. The credential resolver normalises both into the `_connection_credential` metadata slot AuthMiddleware already consumes.

parallel_groups.rationale: Per suggestions-v2.md §Q6 NR-1: phases 06 and 07 MAY land before 04 and 05 once 01/02/03 are complete. Phase 06's edits (conformance_runner.py + conformance.yml + new fixture) do not depend on phase 04's pipeline.py edits because conformance fixtures consume metadata opaquely — the new fixture's pipeline_trace assertion will work whether or not the trace shape has been canonicalised by phase 04 (the fixture asserts on plugin_id/verdict/error_code which exist in the legacy middleware_timings shape too).

03-build-http.note: MAY start in parallel with 02 if engineer capacity allows; both touch disjoint files (mcp_server/* vs adapters/transports/http/*)

05-concurrency-fix.note: Replay-cache race becomes reachable for the first time once auth runs per-request via Pipeline; landing 02+03 without 05 ships a known race window — minimum-acceptable: ship 05 before any production deploy of 02+03

07-server-side-rejection-fixture.note: Landing 06+07 first nails the symbolic milestone (substitution deletion + green CI) on schedule even if 04/05 hit unexpected complexity
